never_side.own_rederivation: filter8.c hurwitz(): returns 0 (dropped) on any negative coefficient, else 2 (B) on a zero coefficient, else iterates minors returning 0 on the first negative and 2 on the first zero minor. So B means 'a zero met before any negative' (alpha >= -1/2), exactly as the agent and the chain_referee state. Both B and dropped are excluded from the limit map; by the Hurwitz theorem any non-positive minor already implies a root with Re >= 0, i.e. alpha(A|perp) >= -1/2, and for beta > 2 the compression eigenvalue 1 - beta(1+alpha) <= 1 - beta/2 < 0 forces instability for all large t, so the exclusion is sound regardless of the B/dropped split.

The float convergence failures are a consequence of slow oscillatory modes near the stability boundary; stability itself is decided exactly elsewhere, so none of the six notes touches the result.

theory_relied_on_and_rechecked: Along the ray eps=1/(t+1), delta=(beta-1)eps one has (t+1)(I-W) = I + tJ + beta N (own derivation, N = J - I - A^T), so x is proportional to adj(I+beta N)1 (t-free) and legality q>1 is beta > 2 + 1/t; the n-1 eigenvalues of I + tJ + beta N not escaping to infinity tend to those of the compression of I + beta N to 1^perp, namely 1 - beta(1+lambda) for lambda in spec(A|perp); hence limit stability on some legal ray iff alpha(A|perp) < -1/2 (Lemma I.3(d)), and alpha >= -1/2 gives instability for all large t at every beta > 2 (I.3(c2)). This is the step that makes the spectral prefilter (filter8 S) lossless for the limit map, and it is consistent with every datum seen (all 9,133 candidates have stable t-sets (t*, inf); 300 S lines all alpha < -1/2; 300 B and 300 non-printed domination-free lines never stable on 240,000 legal points). The e_2 edge bound (arcs >= 29, hence underlying edges >= 15) and Lemma D (domination prune) are Lean-checked.
